original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

actual_scope: For one concrete new helper inventory, the PR2339 400-helper 80-alias T74 words (PR2226 low anticipatory aliases plus 5 extra highs on the PR2269 borrow words), how much of the freed local rank mass survives an actual legal whole-helper owner fill on the unchanged PR2269 T74 template, and what is the width-aware ceiling of any such fill?
scope_change_reason: The card asks generally whether a new local cost interface beats current packing. PR2339 proposed one concrete inventory and estimated (from a width-blind packing cap) a b of about 0.0017259. The decisive question for that inventory is whether an actual legal owner fill reaches it, so the scope is narrowed to that inventory on the unchanged PR2269 template.
bottleneck_link: The complex supplier binds the selected record. PR2339's inventory lowered local rank mass by 121 per call; if it packed like PR2269 it would have raised the complex endpoint above every open T74 claim. This package shows the inventory change is cost-negative once whole helper widths meet the fixed rank-8/16/32/48 bin stock, so it is not a route past the current T74 claims.
stop_rule: Stop when (i) a legal whole-helper owner fill of the 80-alias words is built and independently recounted and priced, and (ii) a certified width-aware ceiling for every such fill is computed, with positive controls on PR2269 and PR2322; no further optimisation once the fill is within 1e-4 relative of the ceiling.
evidence: OWNERS-80.json.gz: 266,400 whole-helper roles, legal under rules R-a..R-g (standalone fill_check80.py, 16 rejecting mutations, PR2269 fill as positive control), certified native b in [0.0016865432362690642682667899981505185179, ...180] (price80.py, width 1e-40). ceiling_lp.py: exact rational LP-dual certificate that every legal whole-helper fill of these words has b < 0.0016867; PR2269 (b < 0.0016965) and PR2322 (b < 0.0016973) are positive controls not rejected at their claims; OWNERS-80 realizes 99.994% of the LP ceiling. PR2360's independent DUAL.json (b < 0.0016870) re-checked. All below PR2269 b = 0.00169624714.
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Prepared with substantial AI assistance: Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the builder, checkers, LP certificate and this text under the author's sprint loop; an independent subagent reviewed the fill checker and added rule R-g. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Is there a low-alias subset (k of the 32 PR2226 low lenders, 0 < k < 32) whose width-9 lenders still pack into the rank-32 and rank-48 bins without remainders, so that its local mass saving survives?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All 32 lows (and the 32-low-only variant) cap below PR2269; a partial subset trades fewer width-9 helpers against less mass saving, and only that trade-off can still help on this template.
open_questions.first_step: Build the k-low words with PR2339 build_ext.py restricted to a lender subset, recount the local profile, and screen each k with ceiling_lp.py certify() before any fill.
open_questions.blocked_by: Per-subset local profiles are not known without rebuilding the words; the profile does not follow from mass alone.

open_questions.question: Can a changed parent bin inventory (different T74 child ranks than 8/16/32/48) absorb width-9 helpers without remainders while keeping the halving guard and deficit?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The loss comes from width-9 helpers leaving rank-5/7 remainders in rank-16/32 bins; a different bin stock removes that fragmentation at the template level.
open_questions.first_step: Parametrise NB in ceiling_lp.py by alternative T74 child-rank stocks with the same rank mass and screen the 80-alias inventory.
open_questions.blocked_by: A changed template needs its own scalar schedule, windows and outer ledger; only the screen is cheap.

open_questions.question: Would splitting a width-9 low lender's reservation across two bins (non-whole helpers) be legal under the hosting rules?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The ceiling assumes unsplit helpers; split reservations are the only packing-side escape for this inventory.
open_questions.first_step: State the split-reservation rule against the PR2269 window and family rules and price it with a modified pattern LP.
open_questions.blocked_by: No current hosting contract allows split helper reservations; this needs a new lemma, not computation.
